The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the first decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. This was the largest push toward failure. The second strongest factor was your Law School Admission Test score. At 25, it is far below the accepted-student average of about 37, and it also pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class standing was the third factor. It, too, places you in the first decile, well below the accepted average near the sixth decile, reinforcing the same concern. All three top factors pointed toward bar failure. Your undergraduate GPA was also below the accepted average, though it was less influential. Your gender and Native American background were not used, and your middle family income and full-time status did not drive this outcome.

To move forward, ask admissions whether an appeal or reconsideration is possible and what new evidence they accept. Retake the Law School Admission Test with structured preparation, strengthen your academic record if you can, and seek pre-law advising. Consider a later application cycle and programs that review applicants holistically, including any explanation of personal or educational challenges.
prompt:

Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission. 
Feature values (with comparisons to students who were accepted where available - showing distribution or average among students who were accepted):
- decile1 = 1.00 (the decile to which the student belongs in the school given his grades in Year 1.) - average: 6.00
- decile3 = 1.00 (the decile to which the student belongs in the school given his grades in Year 3.) - average: 5.79
- fam_inc = Middle (the family income bracket of the student.) - distribution: Upper-middle: 45.4%, Middle: 34.8%, Lower-middle: 8.8%, High: 8.8%, Low: 2.2%

- gender = female (the gender of the student.)
- race = native american (the racial background of the student.)
- fulltime = Full-time (whether the student will work full-time or part-time.) - distribution: Full-time: 92.8%, Part-time: 7.2%

- Predicted probability of failure: 98.0%

Feature  SHAP_Value

   lsat    0.153472

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
1) The model's predicted probability of bar exam failure and what this means for the student.
